declarations.docstring: The canonical linear map from the quotient by `g` to the quotient by `f` and `g`.
The quotient map sends a polynomial representative to its corresponding class.
The canonical map between these polynomial quotients is onto.
Identifies the iterated quotient after imposing `f` with the quotient by both polynomials.
Relates linear maps between principal polynomial quotients to the quotient by both generators.
Identifies maps between the two quotients with the kernel of the induced scalar map.
Under the nonvanishing hypothesis, the scalar-map kernel is equivalent to the joint quotient.
The linear endomorphism of a polynomial quotient given by multiplication by a polynomial.
The linear endomorphism of a module induced by scalar multiplication.
Evaluating the scalar linear map gives the usual scalar action.
Evaluating the quotient scalar map gives multiplication on the quotient.
The kernel of the induced quotient map is the submodule generated by the scalar polynomial.
A nonzero polynomial has trivial scalar-action kernel on the polynomial module.
The tensor product of two principal polynomial quotients is equivalent to their joint quotient.
The positive-degree auxiliary construction for an integer module has at most one element.
In degree one, the auxiliary integer construction on two cyclic modules is additively equivalent to their gcd cyclic module.
The auxiliary construction on two integer cyclic modules is subsingleton from degree two onward.
In degree zero, the auxiliary integer construction on cyclic modules is additively equivalent to the gcd cyclic module.
The degree-one auxiliary categorical object associated with a nonzero cyclic module is zero.
The positive-degree auxiliary categorical object with an integer input is zero.
The degree-one auxiliary categorical object of two nonzero cyclic modules is isomorphic to the gcd cyclic module.
The auxiliary categorical object of two cyclic modules vanishes in degrees at least two.
The degree-zero auxiliary categorical object of two cyclic modules is isomorphic to the gcd cyclic module.
The positive-degree auxiliary construction from a polynomial module is subsingleton.
In degree one, the auxiliary construction between polynomial quotients is additively equivalent to their joint quotient.
The auxiliary construction for a pair of polynomial quotients is subsingleton from degree two onward.
In degree zero, the auxiliary construction between polynomial quotients is additively equivalent to their joint quotient.
The degree-one auxiliary categorical object of a nonzero polynomial quotient is zero.
The positive-degree auxiliary categorical object with a polynomial-module input is zero.
The degree-one auxiliary categorical object of two nonzero polynomial quotients is isomorphic to their joint quotient.
The auxiliary categorical object of a pair of polynomial quotients vanishes from degree two onward.
The degree-zero auxiliary categorical object of two polynomial quotients is isomorphic to their joint quotient.
The canonical integer-linear map from a cyclic module to the cyclic module of the gcd.
The canonical map to the gcd cyclic module agrees with the corresponding cast map.
Integer-linear maps between nontrivial cyclic modules are additively equivalent to the cyclic module of their gcd.
Maps out of a nontrivial cyclic module are additively equivalent to the kernel of multiplication by its modulus.
The integer-linear map from the gcd cyclic module into the second cyclic module.
The map from the gcd cyclic module sends a natural representative to the prescribed multiple.
The map from the gcd cyclic module sends an integer class to the corresponding scaled integer.
The integer-linear endomorphism of an additive group given by multiplication by a natural number.
The scalar-multiplication endomorphism of a cyclic integer module.
Evaluating the cyclic scalar map gives multiplication by the selected natural number.
Evaluating the natural scalar map gives the natural-number action.
The range of multiplication by a natural number is the submodule generated by that number.
The kernel of the canonical map to the gcd cyclic module is the submodule generated by the first modulus.
Every integer-linear map from a nontrivial finite cyclic module to the integers is equal.
The kernel of nonzero natural-number multiplication on the integers is subsingleton.
The tensor product of two cyclic integer modules is linearly equivalent to the cyclic module of their gcd.
A quotient of a cyclic module by the indicated generated submodule is linearly equivalent to the gcd cyclic module.
The kernel of cyclic scalar multiplication is linearly equivalent to the cyclic module of the gcd.
The degree-one auxiliary construction from a nonzero cyclic module is additively equivalent to the target modulo its generated scalar submodule.
In a short exact sequence, projectivity of the first two objects bounds the projective dimension of the third by one.
The quotient by a polynomial ideal carries the displayed module structure over the opposite polynomial ring.
A cyclic integer module carries the displayed module structure over opposite integers.
The degree-one auxiliary categorical object of a nonzero polynomial quotient is isomorphic to a scalar-map kernel.
The degree-one auxiliary categorical object of a nonzero cyclic module is isomorphic to a natural scalar-map kernel.
The auxiliary categorical object from a polynomial quotient and a module vanishes from degree two onward.
The auxiliary categorical object from a cyclic integer module and an additive group vanishes from degree two onward.
The degree-zero auxiliary categorical object from a cyclic module is isomorphic to the target modulo its generated scalar submodule.
